meta: A man once thought to be Spinoza, in a miniature by Johan Michaël Schmidt Crans of about 1840 after a Dutch miniature of about 1670.
about: This miniature shows a man in bust length, turned to the right and facing us. He was formerly taken for a portrait of the philosopher Baruch de Spinoza. It is after a miniature portrait by an unknown Dutch master of about 1670 in the Royal House Archive. Johan Michaël Schmidt Crans made the copy, which the catalog dates to 1840.

meta: Soldiers run past two cannons and cavalry at the capture of guns at Appomattox, a drawing by Alfred R. Waud.
about: The scene shows the capture of guns and prisoners at Appomattox. Soldiers run at the left, two cannons stand at the center, and horses and cavalry are at the right. A group in the foreground includes one wounded man and one lying face down on the ground. Alfred R. Waud made the picture, which is titled Capture of Guns and Destruction of a Confederate Wagon Train.

meta: The bamboo cutter begs Princess Kaguya not to return to the Moon Palace in Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's print of about 1885 to 1892.
about: In the Japanese legend of the Bamboo Cutter, an old man finds a baby girl in a bamboo stalk and raises her with his wife. The girl, Kaguyahime, grows into a young woman and goes back to her home in the Moon Palace without accepting any of her suitors, the emperor among them. This print shows the moment when the bamboo cutter begs her not to leave. Tsukioka Yoshitoshi made it for a series of twelve.

meta: Jan Verkade paints under a tree at Hattem, a portrait by Richard Nicolaüs Roland Holst, signed and dated 1891.
about: Jan Verkade, who lived from 1868 to 1946, sits on the ground painting under a tree, with a board on his knees. Richard Nicolaüs Roland Holst signed and dated the picture at Hattem in 1891, with a note that it is a portrait of Verkade. The artist left it to the Dutch State in 1938, and it passed to the Rijksmuseum in 1979.

meta: A mother receives her new baby daughter after the baptism in Abraham Bosse's Marriage in the City, plate IV.
about: In a fashionable upper-middle-class room, a mother receives her new baby daughter from the child's nurse while children and friends look on. She reclines in a stylish four-poster bed with hangings that match the chair upholstery, and cups with ostrich feathers crown the bedposts. A servant sets a table with tarts and fruit for the celebration. A woven hanging on the back wall shows Diana, protector of childbirth, whose arms are turning into laurel leaves. Abraham Bosse made the print around 1630.

meta: Vasily Kandinsky's Painting with Troika of 1911, in a frame he painted himself, from his Blaue Reiter years in Munich.
about: Kandinsky was a founder of the Blaue Reiter, a loose group of artists in Munich who shared a belief in the symbolic and spiritual power of form and color. They often used a common palette with expressive brushwork and promoted a spontaneous, intuitive way of painting, drawing on non-Western, medieval European and folk art. Here a troika, the traditional carriage drawn by three horses, and the hand-painted frame that Kandinsky made specially for the work show how strongly those sources influenced him.

meta: Arion rides a sea horse against a gold ground in William Adolphe Bouguereau's Pompeian-style painting of 1855.
about: Arion, an ancient Greek poet, escaped death by riding away on a sea creature that his song had drawn near. The painting is one of a series of eight that Anatole Bartholoni ordered from the 29-year-old Bouguereau for his Paris home, decorated in the Pompeian revival style. Crisp cut-out forms stand against a gold background painted to imitate mosaic. In the companion picture a bacchante rides a panther. The works were shown at the Paris Salon of 1857.

meta: François de Nesmond, Bishop of Bayeux, in an oval frame with his arms below, a portrait print by Robert Nanteuil, about 1660.
about: An oval frame holds a bust portrait of François de Nesmond, Bishop of Bayeux, who lived from 1629 to 1715. He wears clerical dress and a simple episcopal cross on a ribbon. His coat of arms is in a second oval below, and hunting horns fill the four corners. Robert Nanteuil made the print around 1660.

meta: The waterfalls at Tivoli with fishermen in the foreground, Claude-Joseph Vernet's likely first major work in Rome, 1737.
about: This is probably Vernet's first major work in Rome. He is remembered for marine subjects, and water is central here too. In Rome he took in the dramatic, rugged landscape tradition set by Salvator Rosa, and the craggy rocks and cascades that made Tivoli famous show it. He blends that with the calmer pastoral manner of French landscape from Claude Lorrain. Fishermen in the foreground and touches of civilization behind them add people. Napoleon's brother Lucien Bonaparte owned the painting.

meta: A wooded landscape with figures on a road over a hill and a river on the left, by Anthonie Waterloo.
about: A wooded landscape has a few figures on a road among the trees, going over a hill at the right, and a river at the left. Anthonie Waterloo painted it, and the catalog dates it to 1640.

meta: Kinokuniya Bunzaemon, one of Edo's first millionaire merchants, shown with a New Year meal in a scroll by Utagawa Toyokuni.
about: Kinokuniya Bunzaemon was one of Edo's first millionaire merchants. He made his fortune selling lumber in a booming trade that fire often wrecked, and he was known for his extravagance, entertaining lavishly and supporting the theater. He once reportedly floated gold and lacquer cups down the Sumida River for people downstream. The museum says this may be an imaginary portrait, since he died in 1734, 35 years before Toyokuni was born. He probably enjoys a New Year meal of sushi on blue-and-white porcelain.
credit_line: The Kelvin Smith Collection, given by Mrs. Kelvin Smith

meta: A man eats his midday meal on a log at a shipyard on the Maas while a woman and child look on, painted by Johan Conrad Greive in 1865.
about: This is a view of a shipyard on the Maas. A man sits on a block of wood eating, with a woman and a child in front of him. A boat covered with sails lies behind them, and several ships are being repaired in the yard. A mill stands in the distance. Johan Conrad Greive painted the midday break in 1865.
